summary: The FIBER11 Consortium, a regional public consortium, urges the FCC to affirm the statutory mandate of Section 254 and reject proposals to sunset or restrict E-Rate support. It also urges the preservation of Category 1 Special Construction and self-provisioned network funding, which are essential for consortium cost-efficiency. The consortium maintains practical CIPA boundaries that respect school-owned device focus while streamlining consortium administration. FIBER11 Consortium opposes sunsetting E-Rate, citing lack of statutory authority under Section 254 of the Communications Act to terminate or restrict the program. The FCC lacks authority to arbitrarily sunset E-Rate under the Communications Act. FIBER11 emphasizes the importance of maintaining E-Rate continuity to ensure broadband access for educational institutions. The FCC must honor the statutory mandate to maintain E-Rate program continuity. The comments argue against restricting special construction or dark fiber under E-Rate, emphasizing the cost savings and competitive value of self-provisioned and consortium models. The comments cite the FIBER11 Consortium's success in constructing a dedicated fiber backbone and achieving lower recurring costs per megabit compared to commercial alternatives.
